h1: An auto parts B2B ordering portal for brands, distributors and retailers
lede: For parts brands and distributors selling to retailers and workshops. Your buyers order by part number, paste a list or upload a spreadsheet, repeat last week’s order in one step, and buy on credit up to the limit you set. They search your catalogue by name or part number. Searching by vehicle is not built yet.

gapsLede: What a parts business will ask about that is not there yet.

faq.q: Can a retailer paste 100 part numbers at once?
faq.a: Yes. Paste part numbers and quantities, or upload a spreadsheet of up to 500 lines. Numbers that cannot be ordered come back with the row number and the reason, such as too little stock.

faq.q: Can a mechanic search by vehicle?
faq.a: No. The catalogue is searched by product name or part number. A vehicle make, model and year search is not built.

faq.q: Can workshops and retailers see different prices?
faq.a: Yes. Put each kind of buyer in a group with its own price list, with lower prices at quantities you choose.

faq.q: Can our salesmen take orders on a retailer’s credit?
faq.a: Not yet. Your team can enter a phone order at the retailer’s prices, but it cannot go on the retailer’s credit account. Retailers place credit orders themselves in the portal.

Yes, for a store in India with a valid GSTIN that sells in rupees: every paid order gets a tax invoice with HSN codes and the CGST, SGST or IGST split, and the invoices export to TallyPrime. There is no e-invoice, e-way bill or GST credit note, and delivery is printed without GST.

sources.label: GST Council: Notification 10/2023-Central Tax, e-invoicing from ₹5 crore turnover
